note: Point-in-time class of every data source examined directly in this audit. PIT-usable means: a value can be joined to a decision made at time T using only rows whose AVAILABILITY time <= T. 'availability' is when WE could have known it, never the event time. Classes: PREGAME_RECORD_STAMPED (record carries its own pre-event observation time), PREGAME_BATCH_STAMPED (only a file/batch time, resolution as stated), POSTGAME_LAGGED_ONLY (valid only for LATER games/events), POSTGAME_AVAILABILITY_UNRECORDED (post-game and the time we first held it is not recorded), UNVERIFIED.

sources.availability_field: observed_at = single backfill time 2026-11-03T17:56-17:57Z for every row
sources.rule: usable for game G only if availability(row) <= start(G); use game-end (start + sport max duration) as a conservative availability, NOT observed_at; never for the same game

sources.source: CBB kalshi-archive snapshots (prices, volume, OI, settlement)
sources.rule: price at time T = latest snapshot with captured_at <= T; settlement known only from the first snapshot showing status=finalized (settlement_ts is the exchange time, a lower bound on availability only)

sources.source: CBB schedule-archive rows (neutral site, venue, start time)
sources.rule: join on observed_at <= T; later rows can change start time/venue, so take the latest row <= T

sources.availability_field: none in the rows; git commit time of each file not checked
sources.rule: lagged features for later games only, with availability = max(game end, commit time); aggregates must be recomputed point-in-time

sources.source: ESPN summary box scores / NHL api-web play-by-play and boxscore / MLB statsapi (live source probe)
sources.availability_field: fetch time of whoever collects it (nothing archived yet)
sources.rule: may only enter features for games that start after the fetch time
